description: Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy (SWREL) won Coal India's auction for the EPC package of an 875 MW grid-connected solar project at RVUNL's 2,000 MW solar park in Pugal, Bikaner district, valued at about Rs 3,490 crore including two years of O&M. Coal India's first solar EPC award.
contractor: Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy Ltd (SWREL)

name: 300 MW Solar EPC Project, NTPC Anta
description: Enrich Energy secured an EPC contract, including land, from NTPC Renewable Energy for a 300 MW ISTS-connected solar power project near NTPC Anta, Rajasthan, with a mandated commissioning window of 24 months from award. Tender originally floated Oct 2024, retendered Aug 2025.

name: 400 MW Wind EPC Project, Anantapur
description: Suzlon Energy secured an EPC contract from Tata Power Renewable Energy Limited (TPREL) to develop a 400 MW wind energy project in Anantapur district, Andhra Pradesh, installing 127 of its S144 3.15 MW turbines, taking cumulative Suzlon-TPREL partnership past 1 GW. Scope includes land acquisition, turbine supply, BoP, pooling substations, EHV line and O&M.

name: 250 MW Wind Order, Torrent Green Energy
description: Suzlon Energy secured a 250 MW wind turbine supply order from Torrent Green Energy (a Torrent Power subsidiary), to supply and commission 76 S144 turbines across Gujarat, Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh, taking the cumulative Suzlon-Torrent partnership past 1,300 MW. Sixth order in the Suzlon-Torrent partnership, spanning Gujarat/Karnataka/Madhya Pradesh; announced Aug 25, 2026.

name: 250 MW/500 MWh BESS EPC, Tamil Nadu (NLC India)
description: Pace Digitek signed an EPC contract with NLC India Renewables for a 250 MW/500 MWh standalone battery energy storage system across three TANTRANSCO substations in Tamil Nadu, valued at about Rs 709.9 crore including GST, with 12 years of O&M. COD targeted 12 months from LoA; turnkey basis.
client: NLC India Renewables Ltd (NLC India Limited)

name: 40 MW/80 MWh Standalone BESS, Kolkata (CESC)
description: ABCI Infrastructures won CESC's tender to develop a 40 MW/80 MWh standalone battery energy storage system at the New Cossipore Generating Station in Kolkata, West Bengal, under a Build-Own-Operate-Transfer model with a 12-year BESS purchase agreement. West Bengal's first standalone BESS.

name: 5 MW Green Hydrogen Plant, Deendayal Port (Kandla)
description: Oswal-Greenzo Energies (a JV of Oswal Energies and Greenzo Energy India) was awarded the EPC contract for India's first port-based 5 MW green hydrogen plant at Deendayal Port, Kandla, under the Sagarmala Initiative, with capacity for future expansion to 10 MW. Expected to produce ~800 tonnes green hydrogen/year; contract signed Jan 28, 2026.
contractor: Oswal-Greenzo Energies (JV of Oswal Energies & Greenzo Energy India)

name: 200 MW Solar EPC Project, Bikaner (KPI Green Energy)
description: Advait Greenergy (a subsidiary of Advait Energy Transitions) secured a Rs 116 crore turnkey EPC contract from KPI Green Energy for a 200 MW ground-mounted HSAT solar project in Bikaner, Rajasthan, to be completed within 12 months. Awarded Aug 17, 2026.
contractor: Advait Greenergy Pvt Ltd (Advait Energy Transitions subsidiary)

name: 245 MW Solar EPC Project, Khavda RE Power Park
description: Gensol Engineering secured an EPC contract from NTPC Renewable Energy for a 245 MW solar PV project at Khavda RE Power Park, Rann of Kutch, Gujarat, valued at about Rs 967.98 crore including GST and three years of O&M. Gensol's second Khavda award.

name: 300.3 MW Wind BoP & Transmission EPC, Ralla
description: Purvah Green Power (a CESC subsidiary) awarded Ceigall India two EPC contracts worth nearly Rs 298 crore combined for a 300.3 MW wind project at Ralla, Andhra Pradesh — balance-of-plant works covering 91 wind turbine foundations and access roads, plus a 220 kV transmission line, both to be executed within 10 months. Two separate contracts dated March 23, 2026 (BoP + transmission line).
client: Purvah Green Power Pvt Ltd (CESC Ltd subsidiary)

name: 10 KTPA Green Hydrogen Plant, IOCL Panipat
description: L&T Energy GreenTech won Indian Oil Corporation's auction to build and operate a 10,000 tonnes-per-annum green hydrogen plant at the Panipat Refinery on a build-own-operate basis, supplying hydrogen at Rs 397/kg for 25 years, to be commissioned within 30 months of award. Billed as India's largest green hydrogen plant.

name: 9.9 MW Wind EPC Project, Tiruchirappalli
description: Renfra Energy India signed a Rs 85.05 crore turnkey EPC contract with Gamma Green Power (an Orient Green Power subsidiary) to install three 3.3 MW wind turbine generators in Tiruchirappalli district, Tamil Nadu; the project was completed and received service connection by April 27, 2026. Small but active EPC-developer pairing.
client: Gamma Green Power (Orient Green Power subsidiary)

name: 184 MWp Solar EPC Project, Agar Malwa
description: Oriano Clean Energy secured an EPC contract from Blueleaf Energy for 184 MWp of solar PV capacity in Agar Malwa, Madhya Pradesh, part of Blueleaf's 200 MW wind-solar Pachora Hybrid Power Project. Part of Pachora Hybrid Power Project.

name: Ambikapur, Rajnandgaon & Korba Sewage Treatment Plants
description: Enviro Infra Engineers won EPC orders for sewage treatment plants (16, 14 and 2 MLD at Ambikapur; 15 and 26 MLD at Rajnandgaon; 33 MLD at Korba), including 15 years of O&M, awarded by municipal corporations in Chhattisgarh. Combined order across three cities; includes 15-year O&M component.
client: Municipal Corporations of Ambikapur, Rajnandgaon and Korba, Govt of Chhattisgarh

name: Varanasi Rural Sewage Treatment Plants (HAM)
description: Enviro Infra Engineers secured two Hybrid Annuity Model EPC orders from UP Jal Nigam (Rural) under the Namami Gange Programme to build 45 MLD and 60 MLD sewage treatment plants with associated infrastructure near Varanasi, plus 15 years of O&M. HAM structure; funded under Namami Gange central mission.

name: NH-565 Davulapally–Mallapalem Upgradation
description: K.C.V.R Infra Projects emerged as lowest bidder for a MoRTH project to upgrade the Davulapally to Mallapalem section of NH-565 to two lanes with paved shoulder, spanning multiple districts of Andhra Pradesh. A separate report cites a Letter of Acceptance figure of Rs 225.72 crore for the same/related award; KCVR is a Hindupur (AP)-based regional road contractor.

name: NH-43 Extension Gulganj–Amanganj–Pawai–Katni Rehabilitation
description: Ramraja Construction Co emerged as lowest bidder for a MoRTH project to rehabilitate and upgrade a 42.4 km intermediate-lane stretch to two lanes with paved shoulders, from Gulganj Bypass (NH-34) to Barna River on NH-43 Extension in Madhya Pradesh. Ramraja Construction is also active on smaller MP PWD road works around Chhatarpur district.

name: Bharat Future City Greenfield Expressway – Phase I
description: Rithwik Projects was awarded the 19.2 km ORR-Raviryal Phase-I stretch of the Bharat Future City greenfield radial expressway near Hyderabad, quoting 3.93% above the estimated cost of Rs 1,665 crore; the adjoining Phase-II went to a larger national firm. Rithwik's winning bid was ~3.93% above the Rs 1,665 crore estimate.

name: Andul–Sankrail & Nalpur–Bauria Road Over Bridges
description: GPT Infraprojects was declared L1 bidder for a South Eastern Railway (Howrah-Kharagpur section) project to build a 3-lane road-over-bridge between Andul and Sankrail stations and a 2-lane ROB between Nalpur and Bauria stations. GPT Infraprojects is a Kolkata-headquartered mid-size EPC/concrete sleeper company.
client: South Eastern Railway (CAO Construction, Garden Reach)

name: Indore Water Supply Augmentation (AMRUT 2.0)
description: SPML Infra secured a Rs 1,073 crore EPC contract from Indore Municipal Corporation to upgrade water supply infrastructure — including a 1,650 MLD intake system, 400 MLD water treatment plant and a 22 km transmission network — plus a 10-year O&M component, under AMRUT 2.0. EPC execution period of 30 months (incl. monsoons); duration covers EPC phase only, not the 10-year O&M tail.

name: Ajmer Rural Water Supply Retrofitting (Jal Jeevan Mission)
description: A joint venture led by RPP Infra Projects won a Rs 365.85 crore Rajasthan PHED contract to retrofit water supply and provide functional household tap connections to 202 main and 355 other habitations across Ajmer Rural, Arain and Silora blocks, sourced from the Bisalpur Dam system, with 10 years of O&M. RPP Infra Projects is a Coimbatore (Tamil Nadu)-based mid-size civil contractor; funded under Jal Jeevan Mission.
contractor: RPP Infra Projects Limited (JV: RPP-BCC IV)

name: NH-502A Operation & Maintenance, Mizoram
description: Brahmaputra Infrastructure emerged as L1 bidder for a Rs 70.18 crore MoRTH contract covering operation and maintenance (including monsoon maintenance) of NH-502A from km 0 to km 87.18 near Lawngtlai, Mizoram, over a 60-month period. Brahmaputra Infrastructure is an Assam (Guwahati)-based regional highway contractor active across the Northeast.

name: Pailapool–Hangrum Road Maintenance, Assam
description: Brahmaputra Infrastructure was declared L1 bidder for a Rs 25.78 crore NHIDCL contract to maintain the Pailapool-Hangrum road section in Assam over a 12-month period.
client: National Highways & Infrastructure Development Corporation Ltd (NHIDCL)

name: Fatehpur Sewerage & Sewage Treatment Scheme – Zone 1
description: EMS Limited emerged as lowest bidder for a Rs 183.81 crore UP Jal Nigam (Urban) project to construct sewerage and sewage treatment infrastructure under Zone-1 of the Fatehpur Sewerage and Sewage Treatment Scheme, to be executed over 24 months. EMS Limited is a Delhi-headquartered mid-size water/wastewater EPC specialist.

name: Koraput–Kandhamal–Boudh Road Widening Package
description: ARSS Infrastructure Projects received subcontracts worth Rs 164.51 crore from Shivam Condev Pvt Ltd for six road widening and strengthening projects across Koraput, Kandhamal and Boudh districts of Odisha. ARSS Infrastructure (Bhubaneswar-based) won this as a subcontractor to main contractor Shivam Condev.
client: Shivam Condev Pvt Ltd (main contractor to Odisha PWD)

name: Hadaf Regional Water Supply Scheme Augmentation
description: A joint venture of V.L. Infraprojects (80%) and H.M. Electro Mech (20%) won a Rs 42.12 crore GWSSB contract to augment the Hadaf Regional Water Supply Scheme in Limkheda and Singvad talukas of Dahod district, Gujarat, covering pipelines, a water treatment plant, elevated service reservoirs and 10 years of O&M. 18 months for capital works followed by 10 years O&M; bid was 5.99% above the estimated project cost.
contractor: V.L. Infraprojects Limited (JV with H.M. Electro Mech)

name: NH-11 Jaisalmer Bypass & NH-70 Sundra–Myajlar Widening (HAM)
description: ABCI Infrastructures emerged as lowest bidder with a Rs 701 crore quote to widen the Myajlar-Jaisalmer section to two lanes with paved shoulders, covering the Jaisalmer Bypass Link Road on NH-11 and the Sundra-Myajlar-Ambasingh Ki Dhani stretch on NH-70, under Hybrid Annuity Mode. HAM (Hybrid Annuity Mode) structure; ABCI Infrastructures is a mid-size regional road contractor.

name: Windlass River Valley
description: A 38-acre integrated residential township in Harrawala, Dehradun, developed by Windlass Developers; SWAMIH Investment Fund I approved funding of up to ₹171 crore to complete ongoing launched phases and accelerate development. ₹171 crore is SWAMIH Investment Fund I's approved funding for completing ongoing phases, not total project cost. Developer self-executes; contractor not separately named in source.

name: Rama Eiko (incl. Rama Eiko Luxury Floors)
description: A 50-plus acre residential and retail community in Shankar Nagar, Raipur, developed by Rama Group, comprising over 100 Vaastu-compliant villas/plots and 112 independent luxury floor apartments across 16 towers, RERA approved. Landscaped by STGK Japan; Rama Group has developed Rama Magneto Mall, Rama World, Rama Life City and other projects in Raipur since 2001. Developer self-executes.

name: YOO Hub Trivandrum
description: A ₹300-crore Grade-A IT workspace at Technopark Phase III, Thiruvananthapuram, developed by HiLITE Group with global design brand YOO and workspace operator IWG; spans 5.37 lakh sq ft, expected to create around 5,000 jobs. First YOO-branded IT park globally; groundbreaking ceremony held June 29, 2026 at Technopark Phase III. Developer self-executes.

name: G Square Seven Hills (Kovai Hills)
description: A 714-acre integrated township near Madukkarai, Coimbatore, acquired by G Square Group from Rakindo for ₹707 crore; Phase 1 covers 406 acres with 3,127 premium plots, with the remaining acreage earmarked for joint-venture villa/apartment development, IT infrastructure and commercial space. Rebranded from Kovai Hills; sits along the Western Ghats edge near the Palakkad Gap. Developer self-executes.

name: Sushma Ludhiana (mixed-use development)
description: A mixed-use residential, commercial and industrial development on a 59-acre land parcel in Ludhiana acquired by Sushma Group, intended as a self-sustaining live-work community along the Ajmeri-Ludhiana Economic Corridor. Land acquisition announced September 2024. Developer self-executes.

name: Durga Shivam Heights
description: An under-construction residential apartment project in Doranda, Ranchi, developed by Durga Developers, targeting the mid to upper-mid segment with 3 towers and about 200 units total. Sourced from a real-estate listings roundup rather than a primary news article; figures should be treated as indicative. Developer self-executes.

name: Shivalik Luxuria
description: A 5 BHK villa project spread over 1.18 acres on Kalawad Road, Rajkot, developed by Shivalik Group, with units in 2,268 sq ft and 8,100 sq ft configurations. Developer profile describes Shivalik as having 5 completed projects in the Rajkot/Ahmedabad region. Developer self-executes.

name: Sanskruti Royal City (Sector A)
description: An under-construction residential plotted development in Rau, Indore, by Pushpa Buildcon, with plot/unit sizes ranging from 630 to 3,500 sq ft. Source-stated possession date (Nov 2025) has already passed relative to today's date; current on-ground completion status could not be independently confirmed. Developer self-executes.

name: Arvind SmartSpaces Vadodara Project (Ajwa Road)
description: A joint-development residential project in the Ajwa Road micro-market of Vadodara with over ₹700 crore revenue potential, marking Arvind SmartSpaces' entry into the Vadodara market and its 23rd development in Gujarat. Large-scale horizontal (plotted) development announced October 2025. Developer self-executes.

name: Gauhati Medical College & Hospital Expansion and Modernisation
description: NCC Limited received a Letter of Acceptance to expand and modernise Gauhati Medical College & Hospital in Guwahati, Assam, with the work scheduled over 42 months including demolition, design and 36 months of execution. Contract value reported as approximately Rs 2,063 crore in some coverage.
client: Government of Assam (Gauhati Medical College & Hospital)

name: Darbhanga Medical College & Hospital Redevelopment
description: NCC Limited was awarded a contract by Bihar Medical Services & Infrastructure Corporation Limited (BMSICL) for redevelopment of Darbhanga Medical College & Hospital, including hospital structures and allied infrastructure, with main construction targeted for completion in 42 months. Contract secured in March 2025 per reporting.
client: Bihar Medical Services & Infrastructure Corporation Limited (BMSICL)

name: Kolhapur Healthcare Facility (General, Cancer & Super Specialty Hospitals)
description: HSCC (India) Ltd, a subsidiary of NBCC, was selected by the Government of Maharashtra to construct a comprehensive healthcare facility in Kolhapur comprising a 600-bed General Hospital, a 250-bed Cancer Hospital and a 250-bed Super Specialty Hospital. Order reported as secured around March 2024.

name: AIIMS Darbhanga Establishment
description: HSCC (India) Ltd, NBCC's wholly-owned subsidiary, was awarded a contract by the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare to establish the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) at Darbhanga, Bihar. Separate AIIMS from the already-covered AIIMS Madurai and AIIMS Rewari.
client: Union Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India

name: NIT Sikkim Permanent Campus
description: State-owned NBCC bagged a contract to construct the permanent campus of the National Institute of Technology (NIT) Sikkim at Dung Dung Khamdong, Gangtok. Education project (permanent campus construction for a central technical institute).
client: National Institute of Technology, Sikkim (Ministry of Education)

name: NIT Kurukshetra Campus Construction (Academic, Hostel & Residential Blocks)
description: NBCC secured an order from NIT Kurukshetra for construction of an academic block, hostel block, residential block, director's residence, vertical extension of hostels/academic buildings and other external development works, under EPC mode. Education project (central technical institute campus expansion).

name: NIFT Varanasi Campus Construction
description: NBCC won a contract from the National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT) for construction of the NIFT campus in Varanasi, including modification of the existing trade facilitation centre within the campus. Education project (institute campus construction).
client: National Institute of Fashion Technology (Ministry of Textiles)

name: IIT Bombay Fast-Track Research & Academic Building
description: IIT Bombay awarded Capacit'e Infraprojects a fast-track, design-build contract using composite steel and RCC construction for new research/academic buildings, targeted for completion in 15-18 months. Education project (IIT campus research/academic buildings).

name: Tata IISc Medical School / Bagchi-Parthasarathy Hospital
description: Ahluwalia Contracts (India) Ltd secured an order from IISc Medical School Foundation, Bangalore, for construction of the IISc Medical School, including the associated 832-bed Bagchi-Parthasarathy Hospital. IISc Medical School Foundation is a private entity backed by Tata Trusts.

name: Baba Sarsai Nath Government Medical College & Hospital, Sirsa
description: Ramacivil India Constructions Pvt Ltd (RICPL) is undertaking EPC construction of the Baba Sarsai Nath Government Medical College & Hospital in Sirsa for HLL Infra Tech Services Ltd (HITES), comprising a 539-bed hospital and academic blocks for a 100-seat MBBS intake. Project long-delayed since 2022 before this EPC award.
client: HLL Infra Tech Services Ltd (HITES), for Government of Haryana

name: ESIC Hospital, Bibwewadi, Pune
description: CPWD awarded Dee Vee Projects Limited the civil works contract for a 500-bed ESIC hospital at Bibwewadi, Pune, covering a construction area of about 666,801 sq ft. Construction was slated to commence a few months after the report, pending local approvals.
client: Central Public Works Department (CPWD), for Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC)

name: DACL Fine Chem Speciality Chemicals Plant
description: DACL Fine Chem Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Diamines and Chemicals Ltd, signed a binding term sheet to acquire about 50 acres in Kakinada SEZ (Auro Industrial Park), Andhra Pradesh, to set up a speciality chemicals manufacturing facility with a planned investment of around Rs 500 crore. Land term-sheet signed June 29, 2026 (valid until June 30, 2027); land cost ~Rs 40 crore, plant construction has not yet started as of the source date.
client: Diamines and Chemicals Ltd (via DACL Fine Chem Ltd)

name: Godrej Enterprises Dahej Plant Phase III Expansion
description: Godrej Enterprises Group announced a Rs 200 crore Phase-III expansion of its chemicals manufacturing facility at Dahej, Gujarat, raising annual manufacturing capacity to approximately 30,000 MT. Announcement dated Feb 23, 2025; exact completion timeline not disclosed in source.

name: Tatva Chintan Dahej-III Greenfield Facility
description: Tatva Chintan Pharma Chem Ltd announced a Rs 200 crore investment to build a new greenfield speciality/structure-directing-agent chemicals production facility at its Dahej-III site in Gujarat. Start date approximated to announcement month (July 2026); exact commissioning date not disclosed.

name: Payal Industrial Park Phase 2 Dahej
description: Arete Group launched Phase 2 of its Payal Industrial Park in Dahej (within the PCPIR), Gujarat, covering 850 acres, with a planned infrastructure investment of Rs 1,200 crore aimed at agrochemical, specialty chemical, dyes/pigments and chlor-alkali tenants. This is a multi-tenant industrial park development, not a single factory; Phase 1 reportedly attracted over Rs 12,000 crore in tenant capex.

name: GACL Dahej High-Purity Hydrogen Peroxide Plant
description: Gujarat Alkalies and Chemicals Ltd (GACL) approved a project to set up a 5,000 TPA high-purity grade hydrogen peroxide plant at Dahej, Gujarat, at an estimated outlay of Rs 67 crore, targeted at semiconductor fabrication and solar cell manufacturing customers. GACL is a Gujarat state PSU/joint-sector company (majority government-owned); tagged Private here per instructions but note mixed ownership — verify ownerType before use if precision matters.

name: KPR Mill Perundurai Processing Factory
description: K.P.R. Mill Ltd's board approved a Rs 250 crore greenfield textile processing factory at Perundurai, Coimbatore district, Tamil Nadu, with an annual processing capacity of 10,000 MT, as part of a wider Rs 1,225 crore group expansion across Tamil Nadu and Odisha. Board approved Aug 10, 2026; expected completion Q2 FY2027-28 per source, end date/duration are estimates based on that quarter.

name: MAS Holdings Tamil Nadu Apparel & Wearable-Tech Expansion
description: MAS Holdings (Sri Lanka), South Asia's largest apparel manufacturer, committed to invest Rs 880 crore across multiple Tamil Nadu districts to expand apparel, textile and wearable-technology manufacturing, expected to create about 7,000 jobs. Announced as part of Tamil Nadu investment MoUs; specific district names and site-level dates were not disclosed in source.

name: Epsilon Group Battery Materials Complex Bellary
description: Epsilon Group signed an MoU with the Karnataka government to invest Rs 15,350 crore in Bellary (Ballari) for EV battery material manufacturing, comprising a graphite anode plant (Rs 9,000 crore), a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode facility (Rs 6,000 crore) and an R&D/testing center (Rs 350 crore), expected to create over 2,000 direct jobs. Investment spread over roughly 10 years per MoU; graphite anode plant targeted at 30,000 tpa by 2027 scaling to 100,000 tpa by 2030.

name: Tsuyo Manufacturing EV Powertrain Plant Hubli-Dharwad
description: Tsuyo Manufacturing Pvt Ltd received Karnataka state single-window clearance to set up an integrated EV powertrain manufacturing and validation facility on 20 acres in Hubli-Dharwad, with an investment of Rs 250 crore, to produce electric traction motors, motor controllers and drivetrain systems. LoI signed Nov 2025 at Bengaluru Tech Summit; state clearance granted around March 2026. Jobs projected over 3 years across two development phases.

name: Honda EV Two-Wheeler Plant Narasapura
description: Honda Motorcycle and Scooter India (HMSI) will invest Rs 600 crore to set up its first dedicated electric two-wheeler manufacturing plant at Narasapura in Kolar district, Karnataka, adjacent to its existing Narasapura facility. Announced by Karnataka Industries Minister M.B. Patil in early September 2025 after meetings with Honda in Japan; construction start date not disclosed.
client: Honda Motorcycle and Scooter India Pvt Ltd (HMSI)

name: Ultraviolette Automotive Karnataka EV Plant Expansion
description: EV motorcycle maker Ultraviolette Automotive signed an MoU with the Karnataka government for a five-year, Rs 200 crore first-phase investment to expand manufacturing capacity, including a planned second-phase plant capable of 1.5 lakh units annually. MoU signed at 'Invest Karnataka' Conclave, Bengaluru, around March 2026; exact plant city not specified in source; current capacity is 30,000-50,000 units/year.

name: Dalmia Bharat Belgaum-Pune Cement Expansion
description: Dalmia Bharat announced a Rs 3,520 crore capex plan to add 6 MnTPA of cement capacity: a 3.6 MnTPA clinker unit and 3 MnTPA grinding unit at its existing Belgaum, Karnataka plant, plus a greenfield 3 MnTPA split grinding unit near Pune, Maharashtra. Project spans two states (Karnataka Belgaum plant expansion + Maharashtra Pune greenfield unit); state/city fields here reflect the Karnataka portion.

name: CCI Group Polivakkam Logistics Park Phase 2
description: CCI Group is investing an additional Rs 640 crore in Phase 2 of its Grade-A logistics park spanning 20 lakh sq ft at Polivakkam, Chennai, taking total investment in the park to Rs 890 crore including the earlier Rs 250 crore Phase 1. Phase 2A (standard facility) targeted operational mid-2025; Phase 2B is a build-to-suit component with no disclosed completion date.

name: Welspun One Karnataka-Tamil Nadu Warehousing Portfolio
description: Welspun One Logistics Parks committed Rs 2,150 crore to develop warehousing across a 260-acre land bank in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, including 107 acres acquired in Karnataka (51 acres Hoskote, 56 acres Devanahalli). Portfolio spans both Karnataka (Hoskote, Devanahalli) and Tamil Nadu sites; state/city fields reflect the Karnataka land parcels announced Aug 20, 2025.

name: NDR Space Ernakulam Logistics Park
description: A new Grade-A logistics and warehousing park with nearly two lakh sq ft built-up area on 16 acres was launched in Ernakulam district, Kerala, with a total investment of Rs 250 crore. Reported as already opened/operational at time of source publication.

name: Haldiram Snacks Odisha Manufacturing Plant
description: Haldiram Snacks proposed a Rs 1,000 crore, three-phase savoury-snack and bakery manufacturing plant in the Khordha-Cuttack region of Odisha; the state government has cleared Phase 1 investment of Rs 500 crore. Exact site location (Khordha vs Cuttack) not finalized per source as of publication; Phase 1 (~Rs 500 crore) approved by Odisha's single-window clearance authority.

name: AM Green Kakinada Green Aluminium Complex
description: AM Green Group signed an MoU with the Andhra Pradesh government to set up a 1 million-tonne-per-annum green aluminium complex at Kakinada in two phases of 0.5 MTPA each, at an investment of about Rs 44,000 crore, powered by 2 GW of round-the-clock renewable energy. MoU signed at CII Partnership Summit, Visakhapatnam, Nov 2025, as part of a larger Rs 54,000 crore package that also includes 2G biorefinery projects in North Andhra Pradesh.

name: BPCL Ramayapatnam Greenfield Refinery-cum-Petrochemical Complex
description: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) plans a greenfield 9-12 MMTPA refinery-cum-petrochemical complex, including a 1.5 MMTPA ethylene cracker, near Ramayapatnam Port, Nellore district, Andhra Pradesh, at an estimated cost of up to Rs 95,000-96,862 crore; the state has allotted 6,000 acres for the project. BPCL is a listed central PSU (majority government-owned), tagged Private/fundingSource Private per instructions but flagged here for review; project targeted for commercial operations by FY2030, currently at feasibility/pre-project stage with a non-binding MoU signed with Oil India.

name: Emmvee Energy Bengaluru Solar Manufacturing Hub
description: Emmvee Group announced a phased Rs 15,000 crore investment to set up a solar photovoltaic cell and module manufacturing facility on about 120 acres in Bengaluru's IT Investment Region (ITIR), with an initial Rs 5,000 crore phase to build 5 GW of capacity. Formalized via MoU at Global Investors Meet - Invest Karnataka 2025 (Feb 2025); land request of 120 acres was pending allotment per source.

name: Aparna Moonstone
description: A premium high-rise gated community within Aparna Deccan Town in Gopanpally-Gachibowli, spanning 22.28 acres with eight towers (G+44 floors) offering 2,088 3 and 4 BHK apartments. Rs 2,525 crore figure is Aparna's stated investment for the project as announced at launch in 2025.

name: Aparna Newlands & Aparna Sarovar Towers
description: Two gated-community apartment projects in Tellapur and Nallagandla, Hyderabad, together comprising more than 2,500 apartments (unit sizes approx. 1,475-3,700 sq ft) announced as a combined Rs 2,425 crore investment. Rs 2,425 crore is the combined announced investment for two separate but jointly-launched projects (Aparna Newlands, Tellapur and Aparna Sarovar Towers, Nallagandla).

name: Sumadhura Gardens By The Brook
description: A residential development spread across 9.60 acres in Shamshabad/Gaganpahad (Rajendra Nagar), Hyderabad, comprising eight buildings with 908 apartment units. TS-RERA registered (RERA ID P02400007022 / P02400004411). Total project value not disclosed publicly; only per-unit pricing (approx Rs 1.26-3.85 Cr) is available.

name: Sobha Marina One
description: A super-luxury waterfront residential development on 16.7 acres at Marine Drive, Kochi, developed jointly by Sobha Limited and Puravankara Limited, comprising 1,141 homes across 12 towers. RERA registered (K-RERA/PRJ/252/2020 and related numbers). Expected completion by June 2027 per developer; total construction cost not publicly disclosed. Completion date is an approximation (month/year only, day set to 1st).

name: Sobha Meadows - Whispering Hill
description: A hilltop residential project in Akkulam, Thiruvananthapuram spread over 1.97 acres, offering 98 3-BHK homes (1,782-2,217 sq ft), with prices starting at Rs 1.85 crore. Total project value not disclosed; only per-unit pricing available. Completion date is an approximation (month/year only, day set to 1st).

name: Confident Nature
description: A new residential launch by Confident Group near Chenkottukonam, Karyavattom, Thiruvananthapuram, offering 2 and 3 BHK units (959-1,266 sq ft super built-up area). K-RERA registration number K-RERA/PRJ/TVM/136/2025 cited for this project. Investment value not disclosed.

name: Skyline Sanctuary
description: A gated residential plotted development on 7.76 acres at Koonammavu (Alangad), Kochi, with plot sizes starting from 1,702 sq ft, RERA registered under K-RERA/PRJ/ERN/067/2024. Possession was scheduled for October 2025 per listing data; actual delivery status as of today not independently confirmed. Investment value not disclosed.

name: Gillco Meraqui
description: An ultra-luxury residential project by Gillco Group in Sector 126, Mohali (PR-7 Airport Road), spread over 12 acres with 444 apartments (3+1 and 4+1 BHK) across six towers; company expects Rs 700-800 crore investment and around Rs 1,200 crore gross sales. Investment reported by The Tribune as a Rs 700-800 crore range; 750 used here as the midpoint, not an independently confirmed exact figure.

name: Motia Chandigarh Hills
description: A gated plotted development by Motia Group at Derabassi near Chandigarh, offering 280 plots (80-133 sq yards) starting from Rs 14-15 lakh, with 27 commercial shops. Possession was scheduled to start from September 2025; actual delivery status not independently confirmed as of today. Total project value not disclosed, only per-plot pricing.

name: Motia Pacific Center
description: A commercial development by Motia Group at Peer Muchalla, Zirakpur, offering high-end commercial spaces, launched alongside the group's Motia Chandigarh Hills residential project. Investment value not disclosed in available coverage.

name: Godrej Properties Indore Plotted Development
description: Godrej Properties acquired a 24-acre land parcel near Indore bypass road for a premium plotted residential development with an estimated saleable area of about 6.20 lakh sq ft, expecting around Rs 500 crore revenue. Rs 500 crore is Godrej's stated revenue estimate, not a construction cost. This is Godrej's second land acquisition in Indore (after a 46-acre parcel on Indore-Ujjain Road acquired in July 2024). Land acquired around January 2025; project yet to be formally launched.

name: Madhur Business Park
description: A commercial development by Naad Group's Madhur brand at Super Corridor, Indore, valued at about Rs 60 crore, planned to offer office spaces, retail outlets, co-working areas and leisure zones. Announced December 2024 as 'set to launch soon'; construction start/status not independently confirmed.

name: Godrej Plots Raipur
description: Godrej Properties acquired a 50-acre land parcel near Old Dhamtari Road, Raipur, for a premium plotted residential development, with plots priced from around Rs 1.44 crore for 45,000 sq ft; launch planned for early 2026. Land acquired July 2025, marking Godrej's entry into the Raipur market. Total project value/revenue estimate not disclosed in coverage; only per-plot pricing available.

name: Rama World
description: A 100-acre integrated commercial development by Rama Group on Vidhan Sabha Road, Raipur, offering over 3.1 million sq ft of retail, lifestyle and entertainment space anchored by more than 1,400 stores. Total investment value not disclosed in available coverage; construction phase (as opposed to concept unveiling) not independently confirmed.

name: RackBank AI Datacentre Park
description: A 13.5-acre AI datacentre park in Raipur built by RackBank with an initial investment of Rs 1,000 crore, which the company plans to scale up to Rs 3,000 crore over five years. Rs 1,000 crore is the initial phase investment; company's scale-up target of Rs 3,000 crore over 5 years is a forward-looking plan, not confirmed spend.

name: Ashiana Amaya
description: A residential project by Ashiana Housing at Dobo, New Jamshedpur, developed under a joint-venture model on 3.86 acres with about 4.64 lakh sq ft saleable area and 230 homes, expected to generate around Rs 350 crore in sales. Rs 350 crore is Ashiana's stated sales-realisation estimate, not construction cost. As of December 2025 the company had converted 92 units worth Rs 145.34 crore into confirmed bookings. Completion date (Dec 2029) as stated by the company; day set to 1st as an approximation.

name: Excentia Tatva
description: Dehradun's first uber-luxury residential project by Excentia Infra on Rajpur Road, spread across 5 acres with 307 low-density premium residences (2,000-4,600 sq ft), backed by a Rs 650 crore investment and RERA approval. Expected to be ready by mid-2029 per company statement; completion date is an approximation (month/year only, day set to 1st).

name: Sun Estates - Sol Reserve & Saipem Hills 2
description: Two luxury villa developments by Sun Estates in Goa - Sol Reserve (16 four-BHK villas priced from Rs 7 crore) and Saipem Hills 2 (villas of 4,000-6,000 sq ft priced Rs 6-20 crore) - together targeted at Rs 320 crore in revenue. Rs 320 crore is a combined revenue target across two named villa projects, not a construction cost; specific city/taluka within Goa not confirmed in available coverage.

name: Prestige Ocean Crest
description: A sea-facing luxury apartment project by Prestige Group on 2.05 acres in Dona Paula, Goa, comprising 106 units (3 and 4 BHK) with an investment of nearly Rs 90 crore; launched February 2020 and possession-ready since March 2024. Rs 90 crore investment figure was announced in November 2020 as part of Prestige's Rs 2,000 crore, 4-project plan across Bengaluru, Goa and Hyderabad. Start/end dates and duration are approximations based on launch (Feb 2020) and possession-ready (Mar 2024) months.

name: High-Tech Pharmaceutical Park, Dighi Port Industrial Area
description: MIDC signed a concession agreement with Maha Integrated Life Sciences City Limited (MILeS City), a wholly owned subsidiary of Ramky Infrastructure Ltd, to develop a ~INR 3,000 crore high-tech pharmaceutical park spread over 1,000 hectares in Mangaon and Roha taluks, Raigad district, on a 95-year DBFOT concession including a 5-year construction period. Concession agreement signed 13 March 2026; construction period of 5 years follows the appointed date, so a firm end date could not be confirmed. Also reported by Tribune India and DSIJ (Ramky Infrastructure's order book disclosure).
contractor: Maha Integrated Life Sciences City Limited (MILeS City), a wholly owned subsidiary of Ramky Infrastructure Ltd

name: Chennai MMLP Rail Connectivity Package
description: Chennai MMLP Private Limited (the Reliance-led concessionaire) awarded a Rs 216.99 crore EPC contract to a PKM Infrastructure-Nagarajan Construction Company joint venture to build rail connectivity to the Chennai MMLP from Kadambattur railway station. Separate EPC package from the main MMLP concession, specifically for the rail spur connecting the park to Kadambattur station.
contractor: PKM Infrastructure Pvt Ltd - Nagarajan Construction Company Pvt Ltd (JV)

name: Indore Multi-Modal Logistics Park (MMLP), Pithampur
description: A tripartite SPV of NHLML, RVNL and Madhya Pradesh Industrial Development Corporation (MPIDC) awarded Madhya Pradesh's first MMLP, estimated at Rs 1,110.58 crore, to G R Infraprojects Ltd (via GR Logistics Park (Indore) Pvt Ltd) on a DBFOT basis for a 45-year concession, with Phase-1 targeted operational by 2025. Contract was awarded to G R Infraprojects in March 2023 (exact day not separately confirmed); construction has continued into the 2024-2026 window with Phase-1 targeted by 2025.
contractor: G R Infraprojects Limited (via GR Logistics Park (Indore) Private Limited)
client: National Highways Logistics Management Limited (NHLML) / Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL) / Madhya Pradesh Industrial Development Corporation (MPIDC)

name: Nagpur Multi-Modal Logistics Park (MMLP)
description: NHLML's SPV DC Multi Modal Park (Nagpur) Limited, controlled by Deltabulk Shipping India Pvt Ltd (which won the concession with the highest minimum guaranteed revenue bid of Rs 365.89 crore over a 150-acre, 45-year DBFOT concession), issued an EPC Letter of Award worth approximately Rs 105 crore (excl. GST) to EMS Limited for development, operation and maintenance works at the park. Overall MMLP project cost is cited elsewhere (NHAI/Swarajya) as Rs 673 crore; the Rs 105.08 crore (INR 1,050.8 million) figure is specifically EMS Limited's EPC Letter of Award value as disclosed on the exchanges, reported via MarketScreener. Concession includes a 2-year construction phase within the 45-year term.
client: DC Multi Modal Park (Nagpur) Limited (Deltabulk Shipping India Pvt Ltd SPV)

name: RIICO Bhiwadi Industrial Area Road Upgrade
description: RIICO awarded a contract for construction of CC roads, paved shoulders, footpaths and RCC medians at Bhiwadi Industrial Area to L1 bidder Hardayal Constructions and Projects LLP, following a financial bid opening on 8 June 2026, at a project value of approximately Rs 37.25 crore. Project value derived from the disclosed contract sum of Rs 372,504,720.2 (~Rs 37.25 crore).
client: Rajasthan State Industrial Development and Investment Corporation (RIICO)

name: Guwahati-Tezpur Highway (NH-15) Corridor
description: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved development of a 135.87 km four-lane access-controlled Guwahati-Tezpur corridor on NH-15 in Assam on Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) Toll mode, including five bypasses totalling 58.7 km and an Emergency Landing Facility near Tezpur developed with the Indian Air Force. Cabinet approval dated 6 August 2026; concessionaire not yet selected. Second major NHAI BOT-mode highway project in Assam after the Guwahati Ring Road.

name: Shillong-Silchar Greenfield High-Speed Corridor (NH-6)
description: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved development of a 166.80 km four-lane greenfield access-controlled highway (NH-6) from Mawlyngkhung near Shillong (Meghalaya) to Panchgram near Silchar (Assam) on Hybrid Annuity Mode at a total capital cost of Rs 22,864 crore. 144.80 km of the corridor lies in Meghalaya and 22 km in Assam; expected to improve connectivity to Tripura, Mizoram and Manipur as well.

name: Aunta-Simaria Bridge (NH-31)
description: NHAI built a new 6-lane extra-dosed bridge over the Ganga river connecting Aunta (Mokama, Patna district) with Simaria (Begusarai), providing an alternative to the ageing Rajendra Setu; the 8.15 km bridge was inaugurated by PM Modi on 22 August 2025. Reduces travel distance between North and South Bihar by more than 100 km; located on the NH-31 Aunta-Simaria stretch.

name: Shopian Bypass (NH-444)
description: The Union government sanctioned Rs 224.44 crore to construct an 8.925 km two-lane paved-shoulder bypass at Shopian on NH-444 in Jammu & Kashmir, to be executed in EPC mode; the foundation stone was laid by PM Modi at Katra on 6 June 2025 as part of J&K road projects worth over Rs 1,952 crore. Announced alongside the Rafiabad-Kupwara (NH-701) road widening project as part of a combined Rs 1,952 crore package; per-project value for the Rafiabad-Kupwara widening was not separately disclosed in sources reviewed.
client: National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) / Ministry of Road Transport and Highways

name: Sonamarg (Z-Morh) Tunnel
description: A 6.4 km all-weather tunnel at Z-Morh near Sonamarg on the Srinagar-Leh National Highway was built by APCO Amarnathji Tunnelway Pvt Ltd (an SPV of APCO Infratech) under an NHIDCL annuity-based PPP concession, giving avalanche- and landslide-free access towards Ladakh; inaugurated by PM Modi in January 2025. Awarded cost was Rs 2,379 crore; some reports cite an eventual completion cost of around Rs 2,700 crore. Inaugurated by PM Modi in January 2025.
contractor: APCO Amarnathji Tunnelway Pvt Ltd (APCO Infratech SPV)
client: National Highways and Infrastructure Development Corporation Ltd (NHIDCL)

name: Green Energy Corridor Phase-II (Ladakh 13 GW ISTS)
description: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the Green Energy Corridor (GEC) Phase-II Inter-State Transmission System to evacuate 13 GW of renewable energy from Ladakh, at an estimated cost of Rs 20,773.70 crore, with 40% (Rs 8,309.48 crore) central financial assistance, targeted for completion by FY 2029-30. Targeted for completion by FY2029-30; implementing PSU/executing agency for this ISTS scheme not confirmed in sources reviewed, POWERGRID assumed based on GEC Phase-I precedent.
client: Ministry of Power / Power Grid Corporation of India

name: Manipur Urban Road, Drainage and Asset Management Improvement Project (MURDAMIP)
description: An AIIB-funded project to upgrade about 547 km of urban and suburban roads across Greater Imphal into durable concrete pavements, with lined drainage systems, utility corridors, walkways, junction improvements and bridge rehabilitation, at a total cost of Rs 3,647 crore. AIIB loan of Rs 2,896 crore; civil works valued at Rs 2,883 crore; covers 547.28 km across Greater Imphal and 77 villages in Imphal East/West districts in 16 Assembly Constituencies, executed in 4 packages. PM Modi referenced this project (~Rs 3,600 crore) during his Churachandpur visit on 13 September 2025.
client: Public Works Department, Government of Manipur

name: Jaydev Vihar-Nandankanan Corridor Upgrade
description: The Odisha Cabinet sanctioned Rs 949.35 crore to upgrade the 9.5 km Jaydev Vihar-Nandankanan road between Kalinga Stadium and Raghunathpur Bridge in Bhubaneswar into an eight-lane corridor with flyovers, service roads, pedestrian subways, underground parking and smart traffic systems; the Rs 579 crore construction contract was awarded to Dineshchandra R Agrawal Infracon Pvt Ltd. Construction contract value (excluding GST) is Rs 579 crore; scheduled for completion in 24 months with a 10-year defect liability and maintenance period.
contractor: Dineshchandra R Agrawal Infracon Pvt Ltd

name: Rameshwar-Paradeep Coastal Highway
description: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved construction of a new coastal highway from Rameshwar to Paradeep in Odisha in two packages (Rameshwar-Konark 4-lane, Konark-Paradeep 2-lane paved shoulder) on Hybrid Annuity Mode, spanning 160.18 km through Khurda, Puri, Kendrapada and Jagatsinghpur districts at a combined cost of Rs 8,300.79 crore. Package 1 (Rameshwar-Konark, 79.4 km, 4-lane): Rs 5,305 crore; Package 2 (Konark-Paradeep, 80.8 km, 2-lane paved shoulder): Rs 2,996 crore. Expected to cut travel time by about 2 hours 30 minutes.

name: Paradip Port Green Hydrogen Jetty
description: The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways approved development of a dedicated jetty with allied facilities for handling green hydrogen, ammonia and other liquid cargo at Paradip Port, at an estimated cost of Rs 797.17 crore, to be implemented by Paradip Port Authority on a Build-Operate-Transfer basis with 4.0 MTPA handling capacity. Approved February 2026 under India's National Green Hydrogen Mission; Paradip Port Authority to provide capital support of Rs 159.43 crore (20% of cost) during construction. BOT concessionaire not yet named in sources reviewed.

name: Nabinagar Super Thermal Power Project - Stage II
description: NTPC's board accorded investment approval for Stage II (3x800 MW) of the Nabinagar Super Thermal Power Project in Bihar at an appraised cost of Rs 29,947.91 crore; as of the Central Electricity Authority's April 2026 Broad Status Report, the corresponding units were listed as under construction. NTPC board investment approval reported for November 2025; EPC contractor(s) not confirmed in sources reviewed.

name: Bagia Cluster Lift Irrigation Project, Jashpur
description: Under the Ministry of Jal Shakti's M-CAD programme, a Rs 119 crore pressurised lift irrigation project (Bagia cluster) was launched in Jashpur district of Chhattisgarh, receiving Rs 95.89 crore in central funding, to provide irrigation to 4,933 hectares across 13 villages. Construction reported to have begun around April 2025 under the M-CAD programme; located in Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai's home district.
client: Ministry of Jal Shakti / Chhattisgarh Water Resources Department

name: Pathalgaon-Gumla Section, Raipur-Ranchi Corridor
description: The Union Cabinet approved development of the 137 km four-lane access-controlled Pathalgaon-Gumla section of the Raipur-Ranchi Corridor on Hybrid Annuity Mode at a capital cost of Rs 4,473 crore, one of 8 national high-speed corridor projects (936 km, Rs 50,655 crore total) cleared on 2 August 2024. Section runs between Pathalgaon (Chhattisgarh) and Gumla (Jharkhand) as part of the Raipur-Ranchi-Dhanbad economic corridor connecting mining and industrial belts of both states.

name: NH-913 Frontier Highway - 8 Packages
description: Union Minister Nitin Gadkari sanctioned Rs 6,621.62 crore for construction of eight EPC packages spanning 265.49 km on National Highway-913 (part of the Arunachal Frontier Highway), covering the Bomdila-Nafra-Lada, Bile-Migging, Kharsang-Miao-Gandhigram-Vijaynagar and Huri-Taliha sections. Sanctioned 12 March 2024. This figure covers only the confirmed 265.49 km / Rs 6,621.62 crore package; the overall Arunachal Frontier Highway (running near the LAC) has been reported at varying total costs (Rs 28,229 cr to Rs 42,000 cr) across different sources, so no single overall project value is used here.
client: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways / NHIDCL

name: Srinagar Power Infrastructure Upgrade
description: The J&K Council of Ministers approved augmentation of the Zainakote Grid Sub-Station from 450 MVA to 780 MVA (Rs 67.66 crore) and upgradation of the 132 KV Pampore-Rawalpora and Rawalpora-Bemina transmission lines (Rs 25.47 crore), together worth about Rs 93 crore, to strengthen power transmission capacity and reliability in Srinagar. Approved during the 6th meeting of the J&K Council of Ministers on 15 May 2026.

name: Mohmela Sirpur Barrage Project (Mahanadi River)
description: Om Infra Limited emerged as the lowest (L1) bidder for a ₹568.98 crore turnkey EPC contract to construct the Mohmela Sirpur Barrage on the Mahanadi River in Arang tehsil, Raipur district, including a pipe irrigation network and five years of operation and maintenance after completion. Reported as L1 (lowest) bidder in a stock-exchange disclosure; formal Letter of Intent/Award confirmation was still pending as of the source article, so status may still be pre-contract.
client: Water Resources Department, Government of Chhattisgarh

name: NH-343 Upgradation Supervision Consultancy (Raipuri Khurd–Padih & Badki Mahri–Ramanujganj)
description: Artefact Projects Limited, partnering with KCS Engineering Private Limited, secured a ₹59.62 crore contract from the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways for authority-engineer supervision of NH-343 upgradation to two-lane paved-shoulder standard across two packages in Chhattisgarh. This is a supervision/consultancy (Authority Engineer) contract for the NH-343 upgradation, not the physical civil-construction contract itself; the underlying EPC construction contractor was not identified in available sources.
contractor: Artefact Projects Limited (with KCS Engineering Pvt Ltd)
client: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH)

name: Iruvanjippuzha Approach Bridge, Kozhikode–Wayanad Tunnel Road
description: Punia Construction Company, a Haryana-based contractor, was awarded the steel bowstring approach-bridge package (over the Iruvazhinji river) valued at ₹73.86 crore as part of the Kozhikode–Wayanad Tunnel Road project; the main tunnel package was separately awarded to Dilip Buildcon, and tunnel construction began in August 2025. Part of the larger ~₹2,134.50 crore Kozhikode–Wayanad Tunnel Road project; the approach-bridge contract value and contractor name are reported consistently across Kerala infrastructure coverage but a single authoritative press release URL for this specific sub-package could not be independently re-verified within this research session.

name: Giridih Bypass (towards Tundi) Road EPC
description: G R Infraprojects Limited received a ₹290.23 crore EPC contract from the State Highways Authority of Jharkhand for construction of the 26.672 km Giridih Bypass road towards Tundi.

name: NH-2 Six-Laning, Bihar–Jharkhand Border (Chordaha–Gorhar Section) – Balance Civil & Electrical Works
description: JD Cables Limited secured a ₹243.99 crore EPC order (including GST, approved change of scope, and price escalation) from NHAI for balance civil and electrical works on the six-laning of the Chordaha–Gorhar section of NH-2 at the Bihar–Jharkhand border. Project stretch straddles the Bihar–Jharkhand border; recorded here under Jharkhand for state-coverage purposes.

name: Landslide Treatment, NH-107 & NH-107A
description: SRM Contractors Limited secured a ₹60.43 crore order from the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways for treatment of five landslide-prone locations on NH-107 and NH-107A in Uttarakhand under the Annual Plan 2025-26, with an 18-month execution timeline. One of three simultaneous domestic orders (from MSIDC, MoRT&H, and NF Railway Construction) totaling about ₹500.99 crore disclosed together; this record isolates only the Uttarakhand NH-107/107A landslide-treatment portion.
client: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH)

name: International Convention Centre, Dona Paula
description: Valor Estate Limited secured a ₹57.9 crore confirmed work order from the Government of Goa (Department of Public Private Partnership) for development of an International Convention Centre, Convention Hotel, and associated facilities at Dona Paula under a DBFOT model. DBFOT structure: contractor bears upfront capex/financing and recovers value over the concession/operating period, so the ₹57.9 crore figure is the disclosed work-order value, not necessarily total lifecycle investment.
client: Government of Goa (Department of Public Private Partnership)

name: Six-Lane Flyover – TKR College Jn/Yatri Nagar Jn/MandaMallaMma Jn
description: KNR Constructions Limited received a ₹235.07 crore EPC turnkey contract from Malkajgiri Municipal Corporation for a six-lane bidirectional flyover connecting TKR College Junction, Yatri Nagar Junction and MandaMallaMma Junction in Telangana, with a 24-month execution timeline.

name: Aerotropolis City Internal Infrastructure, S.A.S. Nagar (Pockets B, C, D)
description: A Ceigall India Limited subsidiary emerged as lowest bidder for a ₹509.20 crore (incl. GST) item-rate contract from GMADA to build internal roads and associated civil, public-health and electrical infrastructure in Pockets B, C and D of Aerotropolis City, S.A.S. Nagar, Punjab, with a 24-month construction period and a 36-month defects-liability period. Reported as L1 (lowest bidder) in the source article; treated as awarded pending formal LOA confirmation.

name: Ludhiana Urban Street Improvement (HAM)
description: A Ceigall India Limited subsidiary emerged as lowest bidder for two Hybrid Annuity Mode (HAM) urban-street development packages in Ludhiana from the Punjab Infrastructure Development Board, worth a combined ₹207 crore, spanning eight months of construction plus a six-year maintenance period. HAM structure: 8-month construction period is followed by a 6-year O&M/annuity period not included in durationMonths.

name: Rigid Pavement & Lined Drain, Imphal East Division (Package 3)
description: A JV of AMRIL (74%) and Ircon International Limited (26%) secured a ₹631.20 crore EPC contract from the Office of the Project Director, Externally Aided Projects (EAP), PWD Manipur, for construction of rigid pavement and lined drains across 122.209 km of selected roads in Imphal East Division, to be completed in 36 months. Ircon International's own share of the JV contract value is ₹164.11 crore (26%); Ircon is a listed central PSU rather than a small/mid contractor, included here for Manipur state coverage due to limited availability of smaller-contractor records for this state. Funded under an Externally Aided Project (multilateral loan).
client: Office of the Project Director, Externally Aided Projects (EAP), PWD Manipur

name: Thana Link Road Upgradation, Rawlakiar
description: Ground-breaking ceremony held for upgradation of the Thana Link Road in Gram Panchayat Rawlakiar under the Jubbal-Nawar-Kotkhai Assembly constituency, to improve road connectivity for local residents. Foundation/bhoomi pujan reported by The Tribune on 2026-08-30 (article dated as published '1 day ago' from research date 2026-08-31); executing contractor not named in source.

name: Kyara-Bhauwan Road Upgradation, Shurachali
description: Foundation stone laid for upgradation of the Kyara-Bhauwan road in the Shurachali area of Jubbal subdivision, Shimla district. Reported by The Tribune (article referenced as ~3 weeks before 2026-08-31, i.e. early-mid August 2026); exact foundation-laying date and contractor not disclosed in source.

name: Harijan Basti-Dhar Sharghal Link Road, Parali Badruni
description: Foundation stone laid for a 1.5-km link road from Harijan Basti to Dhar Sharghal in Parali Badruni gram panchayat, Kotkhai. One of the smallest verifiable road contracts found (Rs 87 lakh for 1.5 km); exact ceremony date and contractor not disclosed in source.

name: Kadiwan-Umladwar-Galhun Road, Tikkar
description: Foundation stone laid for construction and repair of the 5.34-km Kadiwan-Umladwar-Galhun road in Tikkar, developed under NABARD funding on MLA priority. Funded under NABARD's Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF), routed through the state government; part of a larger Rs 51 crore, six-road NABARD package for the Tikkar area. Contractor and exact date not disclosed in source.

name: Upper Jaishidhar-Duganal Link Road, Bharada
description: Foundation stone laid by PWD Minister Vikramaditya Singh for the Upper Jaishidhar-Duganal link road connecting to the Luhri-Sunni main road in Bharada gram panchayat, Shimla (Rural) constituency, with a 6-month completion target. Published by The Tribune on 2026-04-11; contractor not named in source.

name: Primary Health Centre Building, Bholad
description: New Primary Health Centre building under construction at Bholad in the Shurachali area of Jubbal subdivision, inspected by Education Minister Rohit Thakur during a district-level fair visit. Reported in the same article as the Kyara-Bhauwan road story (~early-mid August 2026); contractor not named. Note: a separate PHC building at Tharola in the same constituency carries a similar but distinct cost (Rs 1.78 Cr) - listed separately.
client: Himachal Pradesh Health & Family Welfare Department

name: Primary Health Centre Building, Tharola
description: Foundation stone laid by Education Minister Rohit Thakur for a new Primary Health Centre building in Tharola gram panchayat, Kotkhai. Reported alongside the Jauni school building inauguration and Garavag road bhoomi pujan in the same Tribune article; exact date and contractor not disclosed.
client: Himachal Pradesh Health & Family Welfare Department

name: Government Senior Secondary School Building, Jauni
description: Newly-constructed building of the Government Senior Secondary School, Jauni, inaugurated by Education Minister Rohit Thakur during his visit to Jubbal-Kotkhai constituency. Contractor not named in source; exact inauguration date not confirmed beyond the article publication.

name: Government Senior Secondary School Building, Devgarh
description: Ongoing construction of a Government Senior Secondary School building at Devgarh, Kotkhai subdivision, inspected by Education Minister Rohit Thakur. Reported alongside the Devgarh Panchayat Bhawan inauguration in the same Tribune article; contractor not named.

name: Panchayat Bhawan, Devgarh
description: Newly-built Panchayat Bhawan at Devgarh in Kotkhai subdivision, Shimla district, inaugurated by Education Minister Rohit Thakur to serve as a hub for local administrative functions. Contractor not named in source; Rs 1.5 lakh additionally announced for furniture.

name: Panchayat Bhawan, Jhadag
description: New Panchayat Bhawan building in Gram Panchayat Jhadag, Sub Division Jubbal, inaugurated by Education Minister Rohit Thakur to improve efficiency of Panchayati Raj institution operations. Inaugurated together with the adjacent Community Bhawan (listed separately); article published 2025-11-15. Contractor not named.

name: Community Bhawan, Jhadag
description: New Community Bhawan building in Gram Panchayat Jhadag, Sub Division Jubbal, inaugurated alongside the Panchayat Bhawan to facilitate villagers' social functions. Very small (Rs 18 lakh) rural community building; contractor not named in source.

name: Community Gym, Shurachali
description: A small community gym facility in Shurachali, Jubbal subdivision, inaugurated by Education Minister Rohit Thakur during a district-level fair visit. Included as an example of an extremely small real construction spend (Rs 3 lakh); likely minimal civil works, limited relevance for large material supply but included for completeness per research brief.

name: Adani Bhawan Community Hall, Balimunda
description: A 2,200 sq ft community hall, 'Adani Bhawan', built by Adani Foundation as a CSR initiative in Balimunda village near Dhamra, Odisha, for social, cultural and developmental activities. Inaugurated around 2026-02-24 by Ashwini Gupta (Whole Time Director & CEO, APSEZ) per India Whispers/Odisha Diary reports. Executing contractor not named.

name: Balimunda Airstrip Approach Road
description: A 1.5-km road connecting Balimunda Airstrip to Balimunda Road, built by Adani Foundation as a CSR initiative to benefit over 400 local families near Dhamra, Odisha. Reported in the same article as the Adani Bhawan community hall; executing contractor not named.

name: 173 Anganwadi Centres, Basti District
description: Buildings of 173 anganwadi (child-care) centres across Basti district, Uttar Pradesh, constructed at a combined cost of Rs 20.48 crore, with the handover/transfer process to the Women & Child Development department now beginning. Bundled program covering 173 separate small buildings (average ~Rs 11.8 lakh each) built likely under MGNREGA/state convergence funding; individual contractors for each building not disclosed. Amarujala article dated 2026-08-14.
client: Zila Parishad Basti / UP Department of Women & Child Development

name: 3 Anganwadi Centres, Sudkain Khurd
description: Tender issued for construction of three new anganwadi centres in Sudkain Khurd village, Jind district, Haryana, worth Rs 38.22 lakh. Tender issued (per Amarujala report dated 2026-08-04); contractor not yet awarded as of the source's reporting.
client: Haryana Department of Women & Child Development

name: Industrial Shed for Mehul Roadways, Gujarat
description: Shashijit Infraprojects Limited received a Letter of Intent from Mehul Roadways for civil construction work of an industrial shed building, with the LOI disclosing a consideration range of Rs 4.00-4.50 crore (taxes extra) and a 12-15 month execution period. LOI dated 14 May 2026 disclosed under BSE SME regulation 30. Value disclosed as a range (Rs 4.00-4.50 crore); midpoint used. Exact project site within Gujarat not named in the filing; state inferred from contractor's Vapi, Gujarat base.

name: Row House Construction for Fortune Dreamcon, Gujarat
description: Shashijit Infraprojects Limited received a Letter of Intent from Fortune Dreamcon Private Limited for civil construction work of row houses valued at Rs 3.06 crore, with a 12-15 month execution period, disclosed the same day as its industrial shed order. LOI dated 14 May 2026 disclosed under BSE SME regulation 30. Exact project site not named in the filing; state inferred from contractor's Gujarat base.

name: Toyota Kirloskar Factory Civil Works, Bidadi
description: Sathlokhar Synergys E&C Global Limited received an order from Toyota Kirloskar Motor Private Limited for execution of civil works for a proposed factory at Plot No.1, Bidadi Industrial Area, Ramanagara District, Karnataka, valued at Rs 6.95 crore including GST. Order disclosed 18/21 Nov 2025 as part of a combined Rs 35.40 crore order-win announcement (Toyota Kirloskar, Reliance Consumer Products, Krishca Strapping). Completion was targeted 'before April 2026'; current execution status not independently reconfirmed.

name: Canteen Building for Krishca Strapping, Mappedu
description: Sathlokhar Synergys E&C Global Limited was awarded a civil construction contract by Krishca Strapping Solutions Limited for a proposed canteen building including roof truss works at Building 01B, Logos Mappedu Logistics Park, Thiruvallur district, Tamil Nadu, valued at Rs 1.89 crore including GST. Order disclosed Nov 2025 as part of a combined Rs 35.40 crore order-win announcement. Target completion 'before April 2026'; current execution status not independently reconfirmed.

name: Canteen Building for Komatsu India, Oragadam
description: Sathlokhar Synergys E&C Global Limited secured an order worth Rs 10.37 crore from Komatsu India Private Limited for civil works execution of a canteen building at SIPCOT Industrial Park, Oragadam, near Chennai, Tamil Nadu, to be delivered by January 2026. Part of a larger Rs 366.07 crore multi-client order-win announcement (Aug 2025) by Sathlokhar Synergys; this line item is the Komatsu canteen building alone. Target delivery by Jan 2026; current execution status not independently reconfirmed.

name: SASTRA University Convention Centre, Thanjavur
description: Popular Foundations Limited secured a Rs 19.82 crore order (inclusive of GST) to construct a domestic convention centre at SASTRA Deemed to be University's campus in Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, with an execution period of approximately 10 months. Order announced 20 August 2026; described by the company as representing about 32.4% of its market capitalisation.

name: Compressed Biogas Plant for Sudhishiram Renewable Energy
description: Ecoboard Industries Limited received a Rs 11 crore Letter of Intent from Sudhishiram Renewable Energy Enterprise Private Limited to design, supply, erect and commission a 6-TPD compressed biogas (CBG) plant, to be completed within nine months. LOI dated 18 August 2026. Ecoboard confirmed the client is not a related party. Plant site/state not disclosed in the announcement.
client: Sudhishiram Renewable Energy Enterprise Private Limited

name: Waste to Wonder Park, Khanpur, Jammu
description: Z-Tech (India) Limited secured a Rs 12 crore order from Jammu Smart City Limited for the design, engineering and development of a Waste to Wonder Park (Luv-Kush Park) at Khanpur, Jammu, built from recycled scrap material under the Smart Cities Mission on a PPP basis. Exact award date not confirmed in available sources; company order-book disclosure named the client and Rs 12,00,00,000 value explicitly.

name: Rajendra Prasad Bihar Gaurav Park, Patna
description: Z-Tech (India) Limited was awarded a Rs 13.91 crore order (inclusive of GST) by Bihar Urban Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited for design, engineering and development of the Rajendra Prasad Bihar Gaurav Park (a Waste to Wonder project) on a 10-acre site between Rajendra Prasad's Samadhi Sthal and J.P. Ganga Path, Patna, along with 20 years of O&M. Foundation stone laid by Bihar CM Nitish Kumar on 12 August 2025; the Rs 13.91 crore figure is the disclosed construction order value, separate from the subsequent 20-year O&M scope.
client: Bihar Urban Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited

name: RE Wall Works for NH-45C Four-Laning, Tamil Nadu
description: Z-Tech (India) Limited secured a Rs 16.91 crore sub-contract order from Ekk Infrastructure Limited for construction of Reinforced Earth (RE) Walls as part of the four-laning of the Vikravandi-Sethiyathope section (km 0.0 to km 65.96) of NH-45C in Tamil Nadu, under NHDP Phase-IV on an EPC basis. Disclosed August 2025. Z-Tech is a sub-contractor to Ekk Infrastructure Ltd, the EPC contractor on this NHAI/NHDP Phase-IV national highway project.

name: Sri Madana Gopala Swamy Temple Renovation, Kollapur
description: A tender worth Rs 4.25 crore was floated for reconstruction/renovation of the Sri Madana Gopala Swamy Group of Temples at Jetprolu, including an arch gate at Kollapur X-Road, and associated work at the Sri Laxmi Narasimha Swamy Temple, Singavatnam, Kollapur mandal, Mahabubnagar district, Telangana; the tender closed on 7 August 2026. Contractor not yet identified as of tender close; sourced via temple-tender aggregator listing citing the Rs 4.25 crore tender value and 7 August 2026 closing date.
client: Telangana State Endowments Department (Sri Madana Gopala Swamy Devasthanam)

name: Sri Kukkuteswara Swamy Temple Improvements, Pithapuram
description: A tender valued at Rs 4.08 crore was issued for improvement works at the Sri Kukkuteswara Swamy Temple complex in Pithapuram town, Kakinada district, Andhra Pradesh, part of a wider state-backed push to upgrade temple infrastructure in the town. Contractor not yet identified; value cited as part of a broader Rs 17.06 crore temple-development allocation for 24 temples in the Pithapuram area.
client: Andhra Pradesh State Endowments Department (Sri Kukkuteswara Swamy Devasthanam)

name: Sri Raja Rajeshwara Temple Expansion, Vemulawada
description: A tender worth Rs 61.50 lakh (0.615 crore) was floated for expansion of the temple complex and provision of modern pilgrim amenities at the Sri Raja Rajeshwara Swamy Temple, Vemulawada, Rajanna Sircilla district, Telangana, with a completion deadline of 30 July 2026. This is one of several smaller works tenders tied to the much larger, separately-funded Rs 99.40 crore Vemulawada temple redevelopment masterplan; only this specific 61.50 lakh amenities/expansion package is included here as it is individually small-value and verifiable.
client: Sri Raja Rajeswara Swamy Devasthanam, Vemulawada

name: Community Centre Redevelopment, Sector 29, Chandigarh
description: UT Administrator Gulab Chand Kataria laid the foundation stone on 13 August 2026 for reconstruction of the community centre in Sector 29, Chandigarh, after demolition of the old building, at a disclosed cost of Rs 7.85 crore. Contractor not named in press coverage of the foundation-stone event.

name: New Boys' Hostel, Punjab Engineering College
description: Punjab Governor and Chandigarh Administrator Gulab Chand Kataria laid the foundation stone on 31 July 2026 for a new G+6 boys' hostel at Punjab Engineering College (PEC), Chandigarh, costing Rs 17 crore, with 103 triple-sharing rooms (309-student capacity) to be built within 18 months. Built-up area disclosed as 78,400 sq ft, 78,400 sq. ft, G+6 structure. Contractor not named in press coverage of the foundation-stone event; one industry-alumni source (pecosa.in) cites a higher Rs 30 crore figure for a related/updated scope, but the Tribune's Rs 17 crore figure at the actual foundation-stone event is used here.
client: Punjab Engineering College (Deemed to be University)

name: DLF Mall of India, Gurugram
description: DLF has commenced construction of a new 26-27 lakh sq ft shopping mall, 'Mall of India', in Gurugram at an estimated investment of Rs 2,200 crore, as part of DLF's retail portfolio expansion in Delhi-NCR. Multiple reports indicate expected completion around 2027-2028. Construction contractor not publicly disclosed.
client: DLF Cyber City Developers Ltd (DCCDL) / DLF Ltd

name: Phoenix Grand Victoria, Kolkata
description: Phoenix Mills Ltd, in partnership with Canada Pension Plan Investment Board (CPPIB), is developing Phoenix Grand Victoria, a roughly 1 million sq ft retail mall on 7.48 acres in Alipore, Kolkata, at an estimated cost of Rs 600 crore. Construction started in 2023; expected completion around 2026 per industry reports. Contractor not publicly disclosed.

name: Lulu Mall, Lucknow
description: Lulu Lucknow Shopping Mall Pvt Ltd (Lulu Group) developed a shopping mall in Lucknow at a total project cost of Rs 1,350 crore, with civil works contracted to KEF Infrastructure India Pvt Ltd (Rs 450 crore) and MEP works to Blue Star Ltd (Rs 160 crore); the mall opened on 11 July 2022. Contract values per ICRA rating rationale dated 23 November 2018 (civil works Rs 450 crore to KEF Infrastructure, MEP Rs 160 crore to Blue Star, against total project cost of Rs 1,350 crore). Opening date per Wikipedia (Lulu Mall, Lucknow).
contractor: KEF Infrastructure India Pvt Ltd (civil works); Blue Star Ltd (MEP works)
client: Lulu Lucknow Shopping Mall Pvt Ltd (Lulu Group)

name: Lulu Mall, Visakhapatnam
description: Lulu Group's proposed international-standard mall in Visakhapatnam, to feature a Lulu Hypermarket, an eight-screen IMAX multiplex and an amusement zone, was revived after the Andhra Pradesh government re-allotted about 13.43 acres of land in July 2025, with an estimated project cost of Rs 1,066 crore. Land was re-allotted to Lulu Group in July 2025 after an earlier 2019 cancellation, and a fresh MoU was signed with the AP government; construction contractor not yet publicly named. Targeted completion roughly three years from groundbreaking.

name: Lykli Gurugram (Ingka Centres / IKEA)
description: Ingka Centres, IKEA's mall-development arm, is building 'Lykli Gurugram', an IKEA-anchored retail, dining and entertainment 'meeting place' of about 130,000 sqm GBA, at an estimated investment of EUR 400 million (approximately Rs 3,500 crore). Main construction works began with a groundbreaking ceremony, but the planned opening has been pushed from late 2025 to 2026 per Ingka Centres statements. Construction contractor not publicly disclosed.

name: Lykli Noida (Ingka Centres / IKEA)
description: Ingka Centres is developing 'Lykli Noida', its second India 'meeting place' anchored by IKEA, in Sector 51, Noida, at an estimated investment of Rs 5,500 crore; Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath laid the foundation stone in September 2024. Foundation stone laid September 2024; expected completion around 2028 per reports. Construction contractor not publicly disclosed.

name: Gaur City Mall, Noida Extension
description: Gaursons India completed 'Gaur City Mall', described as the first retail mall in Noida Extension (Greater Noida West), spanning 8.61 lakh sq ft, with a reported investment of Rs 750 crore. Construction contractor not publicly disclosed.

name: Unity One Elegante Mall, Delhi
description: Parsvnath Developers Ltd, through its JV 'Unity Parsvnath LLP' with Unity Group, completed and opened 'Unity One Elegante' mall at Netaji Subhash Place, Delhi, a 4,89,530 sq ft leasable retail development, on 15 October 2025. Project investment value and construction contractor not publicly disclosed; mall received Occupancy-cum-Completion Certificate from the Delhi Development Authority.
client: Unity Parsvnath LLP (Parsvnath Developers / Unity Group joint venture)

name: Forum North Bangalore Mall
description: Prestige Group is constructing 'Forum North Bangalore Mall', marketed as India's first athleisure-focused mall, an 8 lakh sq ft retail development near Bengaluru airport, targeted to open in early 2027. Project value and construction contractor not publicly disclosed.

name: Prestige Mulund Mall, Mumbai
description: Prestige Group is developing a roughly 2 lakh sq ft food-and-beverage-focused mall in Mulund, Mumbai, featuring more than 25 restaurants, as part of its retail portfolio expansion across Mumbai and Delhi-NCR. Project value and construction contractor not publicly disclosed; expected to become operational around 2028-2029.

name: Prestige OMR Mall, Chennai
description: Prestige Group is developing a 1 million sq ft shopping mall on Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) in Chennai, part of the group's plan to build about 8 million sq ft of retail space across Indian cities. Project value and construction contractor not publicly disclosed; part of Prestige's pan-India mall pipeline targeted for completion by 2028-2029.

name: Man Industries Jammu Stainless Steel Seamless Pipe Plant
description: Man Industries (India) Ltd is building a greenfield stainless steel seamless pipe plant with 22,000 MTPA capacity in Jammu, targeting import substitution for refinery, petrochemical, power, defence and nuclear applications. Investment reported as Rs 550 crore in the original announcement; later company disclosures (Q1 FY27 earnings) cite total planned capex of about Rs 600 crore with Rs 350 crore incurred to date. Commissioning timeline cited variously as Dec 2026 and Mar 2027 across sources; commercial production expected FY2027-28. Self-executed by the company; no separate civil EPC contractor disclosed.

name: Man Industries Pithampur Spiral Mill and PU Coating Facility
description: Man Industries (India) Ltd inaugurated a new spiral mill for narrow-range pipes and a polyurethane coating facility at its Pithampur, Madhya Pradesh plant, expanding annual pipe production capacity from 1 lakh TPA to 1.5 lakh TPA and widening the diameter range to 12-120 inches. Brownfield expansion at an existing Man Industries manufacturing site; self-executed, no separate civil contractor disclosed. Exact inauguration date within March 2025 not specified in source.

name: Ratnamani Metals Kutch HSAW Spiral Pipe Plant
description: Ratnamani Metals & Tubes Ltd set up a new carbon-steel HSAW (helically submerged arc welded) spiral pipe unit with 100,000 MT annual capacity at its Kutch, Gujarat site, capable of producing pipes up to 18 metres long in 18-143 inch diameters. Brownfield expansion at existing Kutch (Gandhidham/Kutch district) site; investment value not separately disclosed for this specific unit. Self-executed; no separate civil contractor disclosed.

name: Ratnamani Metals Kutch CSAW Pipe Plant Expansion
description: Ratnamani Metals & Tubes Ltd carried out a brownfield expansion of its CSAW (carbon steel arc welded) pipe plant at Kutch, Gujarat, raising capacity from 48,000 MT to 75,000 MT per annum for high-thickness pipes up to 150mm thick and 18 metres long. Brownfield capacity expansion; investment value not separately disclosed. Self-executed; no separate civil contractor disclosed.

name: Ratnamani Metals Sundargarh HSAW Pipe Plant
description: Ratnamani Metals & Tubes Ltd commissioned a new Helically Submerged Arc Welded (HSAW) spiral pipe manufacturing facility in Sundargarh district, Odisha, supplementing the company's pipe-coating capacity in the region. Investment value and precise commissioning date not disclosed in source. Self-executed; no separate civil contractor disclosed.

name: Surya Roshni Hindupur Large-Diameter Pipe Mill Expansion
description: Surya Roshni Ltd raised capex at its Hindupur, Andhra Pradesh facility from Rs 75 crore to Rs 125 crore to add about 200,000 TPA of large-diameter (8 to 20 inch) DFT mill and coated pipe capacity for water pipeline and infrastructure projects. Expansion of an existing GP/CR coil-and-pipe plant originally approved in Jan 2023 at Rs 75 crore for 72,000 TPA; capex since increased to Rs 125 crore for added scope. Self-executed; no separate civil contractor disclosed.

name: Surya Roshni Hindupur Four-Mill Pipe Capacity Addition
description: Surya Roshni Ltd acquired 10 acres adjacent to its existing Hindupur plant to set up a four-mill pipe production setup adding nearly 3 lakh tonnes of capacity; the first mill, costing about Rs 60 crore, is scheduled for commissioning in January 2027. Value shown (Rs 60 crore) is for the first of four planned mills only; total investment for the full four-mill build-out not disclosed. Self-executed; no separate civil contractor disclosed.

name: APL Apollo New Malur Galvanized Pipes and Coils Plant
description: APL Apollo Tubes Ltd is setting up a new galvanized steel pipes and galvanized/cold-rolled coils manufacturing unit at the KIADB industrial area in Kolar district, Karnataka, with a production capacity of 14,800 tonnes per month and expected to create around 300 jobs. Investment and capacity figures cited from a publicly shared project-filing summary (KIADB Plot 25-27, Kolar). Part of APL Apollo's broader FY26-28 capacity expansion program (also covering Gorakhpur and Siliguri); a dedicated mainstream news article with the same figures could not be independently located. Self-executed; no separate civil contractor disclosed.

name: APL Apollo Gorakhpur GIDA Pipe Plant
description: Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath laid the foundation stone for an APL Apollo Tubes manufacturing unit (alongside two other companies) worth a combined Rs 640 crore in the Gorakhpur Industrial Development Authority (GIDA) region, as part of APL Apollo's planned 200,000 TPA Gorakhpur plant. The Rs 640 crore figure at foundation-stone-laying covered three separate units (APL Apollo Tubes, Greentech Bharat/SLMG Group, and Kapila Agro Industries) so it is not attributable solely to APL Apollo; a plant-specific investment figure was not found. Foundation stone laid September 2025; part of APL Apollo's broader FY26-28 expansion. Self-executed; no separate civil contractor disclosed.

name: APL Apollo Siliguri Pipe Plant
description: APL Apollo Tubes Ltd is developing a new greenfield pipe manufacturing plant of about 300,000 TPA capacity at Siliguri, West Bengal, to serve the East India market as part of its FY26-28 capacity expansion program. Part of a combined Rs 1,500 crore FY26-28 capex program (New Malur, Siliguri, Gorakhpur plants plus debottlenecking); plant-specific investment value for Siliguri not separately disclosed. New capacity expected to come on stream from H2 FY27 through FY28. Self-executed; no separate civil contractor disclosed.

name: KP Green Engineering Matar Galvanizing and Fabrication Facility
